headline: Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize; Ukrainian drones hit Lukoil’s Ukhta refinery ~1,700 km into Russia; ESMA gives EU platforms until 8 Jan 2027 to wind down non-MiCA stablecoins.

stories.title: Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for advancing international law
facts: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay “for her efforts to promote peace and international law.”
Committee cites her role advancing prosecution of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide — including ICTR breakthroughs on rape as genocide and propaganda as genocide incitement.

Career arc: South African High Court judge, ICTR and ICC judge, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, chaired the UN inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory; currently an ICJ judge in the Myanmar genocide case.
287 candidates were nominated (208 individuals, 79 organisations). Prize money is set at 12 million Swedish kronor.
Announcement came Friday morning in Oslo (~11:00 CEST); BBC, CNN and the NYT led live coverage.
stories.whyItMatters: A clear primary from Oslo on a day when Trump had again claimed the prize. The committee’s text is explicitly about defending international law under pressure.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit Lukoil’s Ukhta refinery ~1,700 km into Russia
facts: On the morning of 9 October, drones struck the Lukoil Ukhta oil refinery in Russia’s Komi Republic, about 1,700 km from the front / Ukrainian border (Barents Observer; Ukrainska Pravda).
Exilenova+ posted local videos of fires, sirens and black smoke; Komi authorities confirmed a UAV attack and said drones were being destroyed, without confirming refinery damage.
The plant processes ~4.2 million tonnes of oil a year (petrol, diesel and other products). It had been hit before (Aug 2025, Feb 2026).
Rosaviatsiya temporarily restricted flights at Ukhta Airport; Moscow’s Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky also faced long overnight outages.
stories.whyItMatters: Another deep strike on Russian refining capacity on the same morning Oslo awarded the Peace Prize — range and persistence of Ukraine’s drone campaign, not a one-off near the border.

stories.title: ESMA: EU crypto platforms get until 8 Jan 2027 to wind down non-MiCA stablecoins
facts: ESMA’s 8 Oct opinion: MiCA-authorised CASPs should stop services that let EU clients acquire or increase exposure to non-MiCA-compliant asset-referenced and e-money tokens.
Legacy holdings: remediate ASAP and no later than three months after publication (by 8 Jan 2027). Sell/convert/withdraw/transfer/safekeeping OK for exit; new buys and promotion are not.
The opinion does not name tokens; USDT (and e.g. PYUSD) are the large examples not authorised under MiCA. Private self-custody is not banned.
CoinDesk and other trade press framed it as the hard date on an EU wind-down that in practice started earlier.
stories.whyItMatters: Closes loopholes beyond spot delistings: custody, transfers and advice are in scope too. EU users still holding USDT on licensed venues have a clock.

stories.title: UK and Germany launch an Industrial Tech Corridor under the Kensington Treaty
facts: Burnham and Merz finalised Kensington Treaty ratification in Berlin (8 Oct) and launched a UK–Germany Industrial Tech Corridor linking AI/critical-tech scale-ups with industrial demand.
A CEO roundtable of primes, AI scale-ups and officials is due later in autumn. Backers cited in UK materials include Allianz, Bosch, RWE and Siemens.
Quantum R&D backing rises to €19.5m total for bilateral projects (five more selected projects; ten funded overall).
Also agreed: a counter-hybrid-threat partnership, deeper space cooperation (MoU eyed for early-2027 consultations; SaxaVord launch access), and a Regional Growth Forum follow-up in 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Concrete bilateral industrial-AI plumbing the day after the first Merz–Burnham Berlin meeting — less rhetoric, more named money and roundtables.

stories.title: Tesla offers to rename FSD as “Tesla Assisted Driving”; Germany pushes EU approval
facts: Germany’s Federal Transport Ministry (BMV, 6 Oct) says Tesla offered to rename “FSD – Full Self-Driving Supervised” to “Tesla Assisted Driving” because the current name is misleading: the driver must stay attentive.

Minister Steffen Bilger says Berlin and Tesla agreed in September that the system may exceed posted limits by at most 10%, with the driver remaining 100% responsible; he will push for timely EU-wide approval.
heise: Dutch RDW already granted a provisional Article 39 exemption; seven member states (~12% of EU population) have adopted it. An EU TCMV vote is unlikely before December.
European coverage notes websites/apps beginning to show the Assisted Driving branding; the product is still not generally available to German customers pending approval.
stories.whyItMatters: Naming and liability framing matter for EU type approval — Germany is no longer the blocker on speed offset, but a qualified-majority vote is still months away.

facts.text: BMW withdrew its lease offer for Saxony-Anhalt Landtag president Tobias Rausch (AfD) the day he was elected; the Landtag confirmed the pull to Die Zeit/dpa — a concrete follow-on to this morning’s AfD politics lane.
Ex-chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited Putin at home in Moscow for Putin’s birthday (7 Oct); German politicians across parties called it a “shame” / “bear service for peace” (SPIEGEL / ZEIT / DW).
FT reports SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son is seeking up to ~$100bn from Gulf/UAE investors for an AI-focused acquisition push (talks early; no deal confirmed).
Three Saudis killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid airport, BBC World reports — a casualty update on Thursday’s claimed strike.
